==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=NSubstitute&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Extensions/NSubstituteTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=NSubstitute&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using NSubstitute;

// Verify.NSubstitute: Snapshots the calls an NSubstitute substitute received, with their arguments.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.NSubstitute
// Note: The snapshot has the same shape as Verify.FakeItEasy's, so switching mocking library keeps
// the verified files close.
// Note: The package adds one converter and nothing else: no settings, scrubbers or recording.
public class NSubstituteTests
{
    // ReceivedCalls() is verified rather than the substitute: one snapshot replaces a
    // Received().Method(...) assert per call, and it fails on a call nobody expected too.
    [Fact]
    public Task ReceivedCalls()
    {
        var target = Substitute.For<ITarget>();
        target.Method(1, 2);
        return Verify(target.ReceivedCalls());
    }
}
